relations.rationale: Height comparisons among Cleo, Hugo, and Dev have no bearing on which teams Dev and Hugo are on.
Relative heights of Cleo, Hugo, and Dev say nothing about team assignments of Hugo and Cleo.
Dev's height relative to the crews is unrelated to the river's current.
Dev's height compared to crews does not indicate whether Dev and Cleo are on different teams.
With only two teams implied elsewhere, Dev and Hugo being on different teams doesn't directly determine Hugo and Cleo's team relation without knowing Cleo's team, so it's unrelated on its own.
Team assignments of Dev and Hugo have no bearing on spectators lining the shore.
Dev and Hugo being on different teams has nothing to do with volunteers passing out schedules.
Dev and Hugo being on different teams doesn't determine whether Dev and Cleo are on different teams without further info.
Dev and Hugo being on different teams supports the idea that there are at least two teams, consistent with there being two teams total.
A calm river is consistent with and supports the idea of only a slight current, since calmness implies minimal disturbance.
The river being calm doesn't directly address ease of judging heats, which depends on the slight current specifically.
The river being calm at some point doesn't preclude the wind picking up later in the afternoon.
The claim about the slight current directly restates and supports that this current made early heats easier to judge.
The current making heats easier to judge is unrelated to Ana checking the results sheet twice.
Easier judging of early heats could support Ana's satisfaction after comparing times, as accurate results would make comparison smoother.
Hugo and Cleo being on different teams, combined with only two teams, would place Dev with one of them, but on its own doesn't confirm Dev and Cleo's relation.
Hugo and Cleo being on different teams supports the existence of at least two teams.
Spectators lining the shore for the first race is consistent with and supports volunteers passing out schedules as part of race-day organization.
Spectators lining the shore for the first race doesn't determine whether the final races drew the largest crowd.
Volunteers passing out schedules is unrelated to Ana checking the results sheet.
